feature: publisher-signed local plugin install, disable, upgrade, rollback, and removal
proved: A durable install cannot be created without a valid Ed25519 proof binding the canonical manifest, exact component identity and digest, plugin version, WIT world, publisher name, and publisher-key fingerprint.
Stored packages are bounded independently from the active in-memory registry, and the persistent enabled set cannot exceed the active registry's eight-package and 32-MiB limits.

Normal upgrades require increasing semantic versions and the same publisher key across every retained enabled or disabled version, retain the previous signed version, and serialize concurrent lifecycle mutations.
Startup activation, enable, stored upgrade, rollback, and run reconstruct and hash the exact component; altered publisher claims or persistent bytes fail closed.
MCP inspection exposes content-minimized installed and active metadata but no component, proposal, or signature body and has no install, enable, upgrade, rollback, remove, or Apply route.
Unsigned packages remain explicitly session-only, and no installed component executes automatically.

Independent authors can generate an external Ed25519 key and the exact app-compatible public signature file with a checked-in non-executing CLI; the private key is excluded from the package and report.
